deep.reconstruction:
This page continues the motivation for a p-adic cohomology of varieties in characteristic p, begun on p.12. There, Serre's argument (a supersingular elliptic curve, whose endomorphism algebra is a quaternion algebra ramified at p and infinity) shows that no Weil cohomology with Q_p (or Z_p) coefficients exists for varieties over a field k of characteristic p.

Opening statement. The natural coefficient ring is instead W(k), the Witt vectors of k. For perfect k this is a complete discrete valuation ring with residue field k. Its fraction field W(k)[1/p] has characteristic 0 and contains Q_p. The insertion 'parfait', replacing a struck-out 'quelconque', records the correct hypothesis: for imperfect k, W(k) is not noetherian, and one would need a Cohen ring instead. The trailing phrase, read by the machine transcription as 'par voie Rig. des ....', is unfinished and hard to read; it is not safe to read it as an allusion to rigid analytic geometry.

§3 heading. 'Review of attempts to define a cohomology theory in char p>0. Return to de Rham via Washnitzer–Monsky. Link with Gauss–Manin stratifications.' This is the programme of the 1966 IHES lectures 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (notes by Coates and Jussila, published in Dix exposés, 1968):
- Monsky–Washnitzer formal (dagger) cohomology is a de Rham theory computed on lifts to W(k).
- Its independence of the lift, and its behaviour in families, are governed by the Gauss–Manin connection, viewed as a stratification, i.e. a crystal structure.

Item 1). Use as coefficients, for cohomology in the flat (fppf) topology, finite p-group schemes, possibly radicial (infinitesimal), such as mu_p and alpha_p. Grothendieck says that in dimension 1 this works very well. It yields a strongly improved, geometric form of the duality theorems of class field theory, expressed in flat cohomology, for curves over a field, possibly finite (continued on p.14). He hopes Raynaud will clarify this theory and its local analogues. Per the p.14 transcription, Artin's remark is said to make the approach hopeless in dimension >= 2, because flat cohomology with such coefficients misbehaves in high degrees. Hence the move to crystals.

The mathematical content is a survey or motivation rather than new constructions.
errors: No substantive error. The self-correction from 'quelconque' to 'parfait' is exactly what is needed: W(k) is a DVR only for perfect k.

The flat-duality-for-curves statement was in 1966-67 a programme rather than a theorem. It was established later (Artin–Milne 1976; Milne, Arithmetic Duality Theorems, Ch. III), so 'cela marche magnifiquement' is optimistic as a description of the state of the art then.

deep.surprise_reason: These are draft notes for the well-known 1966 Crystals lectures. Every idea on the page (Witt-vector coefficients, Serre's obstruction, Monsky–Washnitzer, Gauss–Manin as stratification, flat cohomology for curves with hoped-for work by Raynaud) appears in the published Dix exposés text or in the subsequent literature. The only unclear fragment ('par voie Rig. des ....') is too illegible to support any claim.
transcription_corrections: Line 3 should read 'W(k)[1/p] ⊃ Q_p est un corps de car. nulle' (with the underlined 'nulle').
'par voie Rig. des ....' is uncertain. The ink reads roughly 'pas[?] ... Rig[?]. des ....' and should not be taken as a reference to rigid geometry without confirmation.
In item 1), 'propriétés éventuelles [?] radiciels' is better read as 'Utilisation des p-groupes éventuellement radiciels comme coefficients pour la cohomologie (avec la topologie plate)'.

'Heuristiquement, cela revient magnifiquement' is more plausibly 'Heuristiquement[?], cela marche magnifiquement[?] ... en dim. 1'. The inserted line is perhaps 'en interprétant une variante' rather than 'à contourner une variété'.

The last lines read approximately: '... considérablement améliorée, de nature géométrique, des théorèmes de dualité en termes de cohomologie plate, des corps de classes géométriques (courbes sur un [corps, éventuellement fini])'.
